Your box image must exist on the runtime you end up on, so if your images lived on the other one, run coop build once after you upgrade. To keep Apple container, set COOP_RUNTIME=container. co:op falls back to container only when Docker's daemon doesn't answer, and it tells you when it falls back. co:op no longer supports Podman as a container runtime. Install Docker, or Apple container on macOS 26, then run coop build && coop doctor. Auto-detection no longer looks for Podman, and an explicit COOP_RUNTIME=podman now stops with the reason. co:op no longer manages anything on the Podman side, so stop leftover sibling stacks there first: podman compose -p <project> -f .agent/compose.yml down --remove-orphans.

heading: One composition model, direct fork loops
text: co:op removes coop fusion and its mandatory "consult everyone before every action" governor prompt. Presets, named peers, roles and consultation all stay. Retired Use coop fusion <target> --peer <target>... coop <target> --peer <target>...: named peers remain read-only, explicit, and optional coop fusion <preset> coop <preset>: the preset lead, native/consult/delegate roles, ladders, and personas are unchanged coop acp fusion <target> --peer <target>... coop acp <target> --peer <target>... coop acp fusion <preset> coop acp <preset> Plain coop acp again starts automatically with the first signed-in provider, in Claude, Codex, Gemini, Grok order, and its default account. An editor entry can use ["acp"] and choose through the live Preset, Provider and Account selectors. Explicit targets and presets still take precedence, and --bare still requires a single explicit target. Filtered sessions offer only compatible providers and whole presets. An unrelated signed-in provider no longer prevents a supported lead from starting. Before the first launch with MCP after you upgrade, prepare your MCP config files: Make the configured COOP_MCP_FILE a private readable regular file no larger than 4 MiB. Set COOP_MCP_FILE to a canonical path without ... Shared MCP also inspects the selected Codex or Grok native config, so prepare that file the same way. co:op reads Gemini's native settings.json and generates the box's version even without shared MCP, so that file must be safe before any Gemini launch. Replace a final symlink with a private regular copy. Keep the shared source outside repositories, companion repositories, credential homes and ACP session stores that co:op mounts as a whole. co:op leaves an unsafe input untouched and refuses the launch it affects. After you correct the file or source path, retry the original command. A project Dockerfile selected by .agent/Dockerfile or box.dockerfile must now be a regular file inside the repository. If it's a symlink, replace it with a regular copy before coop build. co:op removes Fleet's commands, its live board and its .agent/fleet.yaml parser. Use the direct fork and loop commands: Retired Use coop fleet init / .agent/fleet.yaml No manifest. Start each fork explicitly with coop fork <name> <target|preset> --loop -d --tasks <path>. co:op doesn't delete an existing ignored file, so remove it manually after you translate its entries. coop fleet up Run the direct detached fork command once per worker. Point workers at the same canonical queue, or use --tasks <path> only to select a genuinely separate canonical queue. coop fleet down coop fork stop <name> for each running fork. coop fleet watch coop tasks watch for merged task progress, coop fork ls for fork state and cost, and coop fork logs -f for output. coop fleet prune coop fork rm <name> for each obsolete fork (--yes confirms without a prompt, and --force separately overrides the protection for dirty or unmerged forks). coop fork merge --all still lands every fork through a rebase queue that checks each fork again. There's no batch up/down command, so start and stop each worker explicitly. co:op also no longer inspects or removes Compose projects named only after the folder, which date from before project names included a hash for each workspace. Finish or stop sibling services before you upgrade. If one of those old stacks remains afterwards, inspect it with docker compose ls, then run docker compose -p <legacy-project> -f .agent/compose.yml down --remove-orphans. When you re-enter a fork session, co:op uses one record, .coop/session.<provider>.<account>. It ignores the older provider-only .coop/session.<provider> file, which you can remove whenever you like, and no longer adopts the latest Codex session by working directory. The first re-entry without a current exact hint starts a new conversation. When the provider creates one unambiguous session, co:op records an exact hint for later resumes. coop init now maintains only the current scaffold, and doesn't rewrite files that versions before v8 generated. If you're upgrading from a version older than v8, make these changes yourself: In .githooks/prepare-commit-msg, replace $HOME/.config/coop/git-hooks/prepare-commit-msg with $HOME/.coop-git-hooks/prepare-commit-msg, then run chmod +x .githooks/prepare-commit-msg. If .agent/rules/ exists, run mkdir -p .agent/kb and git mv .agent/rules .agent/kb/rules so the rule cards stay tracked at their current path. Then update project-owned instructions, such as AGENTS.md, to refer to .agent/kb/rules/. In .gitignore, remove the old co:op stanza that contains .agent/* or **/.agent/* together with !.agent/rules/ or !**/.agent/rules/. Then run coop init once to append the current monorepo-aware stanza. Existing project-owned hooks and custom hook paths stay protected. Instead of overwriting them, init describes how to chain co:op's current hook. Audit-reopen records also support only the current formats. No tagged co:op release wrote the retired v1/v2 formats, so upgrades between released versions need no conversion. The now-unused coop tasks unblock --adopt-audit-head bridge has no replacement. If an untagged developer build left a v1/v2 record, reconcile that task with the build that wrote it before you upgrade. Current co:op leaves the record intact and refuses to lease, complete or unblock the task. Don't delete raw task-authority registry files to get around that refusal.

heading: The /sweep Stop hook in older repos
text: The /sweep skill's Stop hook keeps only an active sweep running and holds no other session open. New projects get this setup from coop init, but init preserves existing files, so update a repo set up by an older co:op by hand: Remove only the stock Stop group from .claude/settings.json. Keep PreToolUse and custom hooks. Delete .claude/hooks/stop-guard.sh, but only if it's the old stock guard. Remove a stale .agent/active. Merge the current .agent/skills/sweep/ files, keeping your local customizations.
